text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This is a non-review research article focused primarily on land use and land cover (LULC) future prediction and simulation at the national scale for the conterminous U.S. The paper details the development and parameterization of a spatially-explicit state-and-transition simulation model (LUCAS) for LULC and associated carbon dynamics. It implements multiple future scenarios (e.g., IPCC-SRES A1B) with quantitative spatial outputs of LULC projections. The modeling is national in scope with seamless inputs and outputs at 1-km resolution, allowing for subsetting by ecoregion or region (e.g., Mediterranean California). Quantitative verification is provided comparing modeled area targets to inputs, and sensitivity analyses illustrate spatial uncertainty and transition probabilities. The model produces mapped outputs of LULC change and incorporates spatial multipliers to constrain spatial allocation. The study includes quantitative accuracy metrics (e.g., R² for area targets), spatially-explicit modeling, and multiple scenario implementations, fulfilling all core inclusion criteria. It is not a review article, nor does it meet any exclusion criteria such as local/regional only focus, lack of future projections, or absence of spatially explicit outputs.)
